Classification guard: the DIRECT_CAUSATION classification follows the ulcer-to-stricture mechanical precedents (peptic-ulcer-disease family and the Pregun 2009 finding that healing the coexistent esophagitis reduces stricture dilation need); the edge is scoped to documented esophagitis with fibrotic stricture outcome, not to transient reflux symptoms.
governanceNotes: D1 batch 31 (2026-09-23): one DIRECT_CAUSATION esophageal-stricture edge authored from the esophagitis-to-stricture outcome literature - the Pregun 2009 review documents acid-suppressive healing of esophagitis as essential to peptic-stricture outcome (reducing repeated dilations), the Cohen 2021 100-patient series documents reflux esophagitis ulcers as the principal stricture source, and the Pearson 2010 30-year pediatric series documents untreated reflux esophagitis progressing to refractory strictures; the fibrotic-repair mechanism is the injury-healing-scar sequence.

Duplicate-scope note: the gerd identity carries respiratory-target edges (asthma, bronchiectasis, copd, interstitial-lung-disease, pulmonary-fibrosis, respiratory-cancer, tuberculosis) and carries no esophageal-stricture edge, so this esophagitis-mediated pathway is not a parallel pathway; gerd-to-esophagitis is upstream etiology and esophagitis-to-stricture is the injury-healing outcome, keeping each edge on its own mechanism.

nexusClaim.etiologicalTrigger: Documented esophagitis (reflux, infectious, pill-induced, or eosinophilic) with mucosal injury -> ulceration and inflammation extending to the submucosa -> fibrotic repair with collagen deposition and circumferential scar contracture -> fixed esophageal stricture.
nexusClaim.mechanismSummary: The Pregun 2009 review documents that healing the coexistent esophagitis is essential to peptic-stricture outcome - acid-suppressive therapy reduces repeated dilations, demonstrating the inflammation-to-stricture dependency; the Cohen 2021 series documents reflux esophagitis ulcers as the principal source of chronic stricture, and the Pearson 2010 series documents reflux esophagitis progressing to refractory strictures in 114 children; the injury-to-scar sequence is the accepted biology.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized injury-fibrosis-stricture pathway: repeated mucosal injury (acid-peptic, infectious, pill, or eosinophilic inflammation) produces ulcers that extend into the submucosa; wound repair deposits collagen, and myofibroblast-mediated circumferential contraction of the scar narrows the lumen into a fixed stricture; durable acid suppression or inflammation control halts the cycle, which is why healing esophagitis reduces dilation requirements. Individual claims require documented inflammation preceding documented narrowing.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The direct classification applies where esophagitis is endoscopically documented before or at stricture diagnosis and other stricture etiologies are excluded: caustic and radiation strictures have their own injury histories, malignancy must be excluded by biopsy, and eosinophilic esophagitis produces both inflammatory and fibrostenotic phenotypes that require separate documentation; no VA probability language is asserted.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Endoscopically documented esophagitis (grade, etiology) with chronology preceding the stricture; endoscopic or radiographic documentation of the stricture; biopsy excluding malignancy; documentation of inflammatory activity control or its absence; exclusion of caustic, radiation, and anastomotic injury histories; gastroenterology assessment of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Esophageal malignancy at the stricture site
Caustic ingestion or radiation exposure history
Eosinophilic esophagitis as an independent fibrostenotic driver
Pill-induced injury with independent scar formation

suggestions.rationale: Authored at DIRECT_CAUSATION: the injury-healing-scar sequence is the accepted biology of peptic and ulcerative strictures, and the Pregun review demonstrates the inflammation-dependency through treatment response; the claim is scoped to documented esophagitis with malignancy excluded.
